- I found no:

  - `public/`
  - `assets/`
  - `index.html`
  - game runtime or level definitions
- Search results show only helper/agent files, not a game app.

Closest relevant framework/code:
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/SKILL.md`
  - This is a skill description for loading and verifying GLB models in a browser.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/assets/viewer/index.html`
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/assets/viewer/main.js`
  - These are the closest thing to an engine/runtime entry point: they use Three.js and a browser canvas renderer, with camera, animation, and scene setup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/Agents.md`
  - This is process guidance for browser/WebGPU capture and game testing, not gameplay code.

What this means:
- There is no existing “game framework” for a real level system in this repository.
- The only engine-like foundation is a browser-based Three.js viewer pattern, not a game loop or level registry.
- So the repo is not yet a playable game; it is more of a tooling/agent workspace.

Recommendation for a complete new level inspired by The Last Run:
- If this repo is intended to become a game later, the cleanest place is to add a new gameplay module alongside the Three.js-based viewer structure, ideally in a new top-level game folder such as:
  - `src/game/levels/the-last-run/`
  - or `levels/the-last-run-escape/`
- Register the level in the main app boot flow (typically a `main.js`, `game.js`, `levelRegistry.js`, or equivalent), but there is no such existing file here, so this would be a greenfield implementation.
- Use the Three.js viewer asset structure as the base for scene creation, camera, lighting, and runtime updates:
  - create a 3D ground path / corridor / checkpoint sequence
  - add hazards (laser gates, drones, closing walls)
  - add a simple player controller with movement, sprint, and dodge
  - add a timer/escape objective and fail states

Specific level concept:
- Theme: “The Last Run: District Shutdown”
- Objective: escape an overrun metro undercity while the city collapses behind you.
- New mechanic: “pulse drift”
  - The player can trigger a brief EMP-like pulse that disables hazard drones and briefly slows moving barriers for 2–3 seconds.
  - This adds a tactical timing layer without requiring complex physics.
- Harder challenge:
  - Shorter safe windows
  - More aggressive patrols
  - More compressed route choices
  - One-hit hazards with no checkpoints in the final stretch
  - Faster time pressure than a standard chase level

Implementation structure I’d recommend:
- `src/game/levels/the-last-run-escape/level.js`
  - spawn world geometry, hazards, checkpoints, objectives
- `src/game/levels/the-last-run-escape/mechanics.js`
  - pulse-drift logic and hazard interaction
- `src/game/levels/the-last-run-escape/data.js`
  - level path, obstacle timings, enemy patrol layouts
- `src/game/levelRegistry.js` or equivalent
  - register the level and load it from the main boot scene
- `src/main.js` or boot file
  - create the Three.js renderer and switch to the new level

Best fit for this repo:
- Since the only confirmed engine is Three.js-based browser code, I would build the new level using that same pattern, starting from:
  - `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs/assets/viewer/main.js`
  - and adapting its `Scene`, `Camera`, `Renderer`, and animation loop to a gameplay state machine.

One important note:
- This repo does not currently contain the actual game project to patch. There is no implemented main gameplay app, so I would not recommend editing files in this checkout until the actual game framework is added. This is a concept/design recommendation only, based on the repo as it exists today.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable game inspired by *The Last Run*, with a new level, a new mechanic, and a more brutal challenge.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- The repository had no existing game, so create a self-contained browser game in `index.html`.
- Build “LAST RUN: BLACKOUT,” a 3-lane escape runner with two lives, no checkpoints, a 1,600 m extraction goal, and a Blackout pulse that briefly slows hazards and disables nearby drones.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game, desktop keyboard controls, mobile touch/swipe controls, HUD, scoring, best distance, hazards, pause, win/loss states, and restart.
- Added play instructions to `README.md`.
- JavaScript syntax check passed; browser testing showed no game console errors.
- Tested the title screen and active gameplay in Chromium.

### Active
- Validate the latest projection adjustment, which brings hazards into alignment with the runner near collision distance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Capture/check gameplay after the latest projection change.
2. Summarize the finished game and launch instructions; note that this is a greenfield implementation because no existing game was present.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete playable game.
- `README.md`: Game overview and launch/control instructions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. `README.md` is modified; `index.html` is new. Other untracked scaffolding files were present before the game work.
- Local server is running on port `3002`; browser viewport was resized to `1050x656` just before the summary.
